hints.title: Interval Bucketing
hints.text: Each interval consists of 6 minutes: minutes 1 to 6 belong to interval 1, 7 to 12 belong to interval 2.

hints.title: Grouping and Sorting
hints.text: Group by interval_no, sum order_count as total_orders, and order ascending by interval_no.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    CEIL(minute / 6.0) AS interval_no,
    SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY interval_no
ORDER BY interval_no ASC;
```

variables: N: number of records in Orders table
complexity.notes: Grouping by arithmetic interval and sorting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating recursive CTEs is unnecessarily complex.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use arithmetic expression CEIL(minute / 6.0) in GROUP BY.

solutions.code:
SELECT 
    CEIL(minute / 6.0) AS interval_no,
    SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY interval_no
ORDER BY interval_no ASC;

SELECT 
    CEIL(minute / 6.0) AS interval_no,
    SUM(order_count) AS total_orders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY interval_no
ORDER BY interval_no ASC;

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def calculate_orders(orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    orders["interval_no"] = np.ceil(orders["minute"] / 6.0).astype(int)
    res = orders.groupby("interval_no")["order_count"].sum().reset_index()
    res = res.rename(columns={"order_count": "total_orders"})
    return res.sort_values("interval_no")
